generation.explanation: The discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac is the part under the square root in the quadratic formula x = (−b ± √Δ)/(2a). If Δ > 0, ± gives two different real roots and the parabola crosses the x-axis twice. If Δ = 0, ± adds nothing, so there is one repeated root and the vertex just touches the axis. If Δ < 0, a negative number has no real square root, so the parabola never reaches the x-axis. Move the a, b, c sliders to see this (a = 1, b = 2, c = 1 gives Δ = 0 exactly).
